/-!
# Erdős Problem 6

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/6](https://www.erdosproblems.com/6)
- [BFT15] Banks, William D. and Freiberg, Tristan and Turnage-Butterbaugh, Caroline L., Consecutive primes in tuples. Acta Arith. (2015), 261-266.
- [Ma15] Maynard, James, Small gaps between primes. Ann. of Math. (2) (2015), 383-413.
-/

namespace Erdos6

/--
There are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < d_{n+2}$, where $d$
denotes the prime gap function.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_6 :
    {n | primeGap n < primeGap (n + 1) ∧ primeGap (n + 1) < primeGap (n + 2)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n < d_{n+1} < \dots < d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_6.variants.increasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) < primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry


/--
For all $m$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that $d_n > d_{n+1} \dots > d_{n+m}$,
where $d$ denotes the prime gap function.

Proved by Banks, Freiberg, and Turnage-Butterbaugh [BFT15] with an application of the
Maynard-Tao machinery concerning bounded gaps between primes [Ma15]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_6.variants.decreasing (m : ℕ) :
    {n | ∀ i ∈ Finset.range m, primeGap (n + i) > primeGap (n + i + 1)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos6

reformulations.difference: The website states the variant for m ≥ 1, whereas Lean allows every natural m. Compared with BFT’s formulation using L ≥ 2 gaps, Lean counts m adjacent comparisons, hence m + 1 gaps.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Finset.range m contains exactly the indices 0 ≤ i < m, so its comparisons specify the chain from primeGap n through primeGap (n + m). These are equivalent to strict monotonicity of the m + 1 gaps. For m = 0 the condition is empty and the occurrence set is all of ℕ, which is infinite. Thus including zero adds only a true case, and BFT’s length convention is recovered by L = m + 1. Both the length reindexing and the equivalence with restricting m ≥ 1 were proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: As in the increasing variant, Lean includes m = 0 and counts adjacent comparisons rather than BFT’s number of gaps.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The m successor comparisons with > are equivalent to strict antitonicity of the m + 1 consecutive gaps. Reindexing by L = m + 1 gives BFT’s decreasing-run statement. At m = 0 the occurrence set is all of ℕ, so the additional case does not strengthen the website’s assertion for m ≥ 1. These equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

review.notes: All three declarations faithfully state the cited claims. The source records an affirmative solution, consistent with every research solved tag. The zero-indexed prime enumeration merely shifts occurrence indices; its fallback value is unreachable because there are infinitely many primes, and its strict increase makes natural subtraction appropriate. Lean checks verified positivity of every primeGap, the m = 0, 1, 2 cases, index-shift invariance of infinitude, and concrete runs (2,4,6) at index 6 and (6,4,2) at index 10. Both scratch files compiled successfully; the named equivalence proofs have no sorry dependencies. The reviewed file was not modified.
